extracted.intended_audience: members of the public, banking organizations, industry stakeholders, and other interested commenters to the Federal Reserve's proposed rulemaking
extracted.subtask_description: Submit public comments on the Federal Reserve's proposed rule to prohibit use of reputation risk in supervision and to codify a policy preventing encouragement or compulsion of banks to condition services based on political/religious beliefs or lawful activities. Includes procedural submission instructions, specific questions the Board requests input on, and the proposed regulatory text and definitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comment submission deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments must be received on or before April 27, 2026.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments received after this date will not be considered. See DATES section for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to submit comments and required identifiers
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit comments identified by Docket No. R-1884 and RIN 7100-AH17 by agency website, mail, hand delivery/courier, or email.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preferred method: Agency Website https://www.federalreserve.gov/apps/proposals/. Mail or hand delivery to Deputy Secretary at Board address. Email to publiccomments@frb.gov and include the docket number in the subject line. Follow the instructions for submitting comments, including attachments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public disclosure and confidentiality of comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments received are subject to public disclosure and generally will be made available on the Board's website without change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not include confidential, contact, or other identifying information that would be inappropriate for public disclosure. Comments may also be viewed electronically or in person in Room M-4365A during Federal business weekdays between 9 a.m. and 5 p.m.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for comment — references to reputation risk
rubrics_metrics.description: Question 1: What other references to reputation risk in the Board's regulations or its supervisory programs should be addressed by the proposal? How should the Board address those references?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide specific locations (regulatory citations, manuals, guidance) and suggested approaches for addressing/removing or revising references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for comment — definition of 'reputation risk'
rubrics_metrics.description: Question 2: Is the proposal's definition of 'reputation risk' appropriate; why or why not? What are the advantages and disadvantages of the definition? How should the definition be broadened or narrowed? What different definition of reputation risk should the Board consider?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss trade-offs of clarity, scope, and operationalizability; propose alternative wording and explain implications for supervision and institutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for comment — definition of 'banking organization'
rubrics_metrics.description: Question 3: What changes to the proposal's definition of 'banking organization' should the Board consider? Should the Board consider including additional or fewer categories of entities? For example, consider including 'permitted payment stablecoin issuers' as defined in 12 U.S.C. 5901(23) after required rulemakings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify specific entity categories to include/exclude and rationale, considering statutory context and supervisory scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for comment — clarity of regulatory text
rubrics_metrics.description: Question 4: Is the proposal's regulatory text that would codify a prohibition on the use of reputation risk clear; why or why not? How could 'examination programs' or 'materials used for the supervision of banking organizations' be defined further?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggest precise definitional language or structural edits to improve enforceability and minimize ambiguity in examination scope and supervisory materials (e.g., examination manuals, guidance documents, training materials).

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for comment — rule of construction (applicable law list)
rubrics_metrics.description: Question 5: What, if any, additional provisions of applicable law should the proposal's rule of construction include in its list? Which, if any, provisions of applicable law should be removed? Why would any such addition or removal be appropriate?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommend statutes or authorities to add/remove from the enumerated list and explain how that affects Board authority and interactions with other legal obligations (sanctions, BSA, ECOA, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for comment — unintended consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Question 6: What, if any, unintended consequences for the Board or Board-supervised banking organizations may result from the proposal, including codifying the removal of reputation risk from the Board's supervisory programs and materials?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe potential operational, supervisory, market, compliance, safety-and-soundness, or legal consequences and provide evidence or examples where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for comment — alternatives to the proposal
rubrics_metrics.description: Question 7: What, if any, alternatives are there to the proposal that would better achieve the Board's objectives?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide alternative regulatory approaches (narrower, broader, procedural safeguards, guidance changes) and explain comparative advantages and drawbacks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for comment — related references in supervisory materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Question 8: What, if any, references to concepts related to reputation risk should the Board consider revising in its supervisory materials or regulations?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify related terms or frameworks (e.g., consumer compliance risk, safety-and-soundness frameworks) and suggest specific revisions or deletions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for comment — unidentified costs and benefits
rubrics_metrics.description: Question 9: Please describe any costs, benefits, or other effects of the proposal that the Board has not identified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide empirical data or reasoned analysis quantifying or describing additional impacts on institutions, markets, consumers, or the Board.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'reputation risk' (proposed)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reputation risk is defined as 'the potential that negative publicity regarding a banking organization's business practices, whether true or not, will cause a decline in the banking organization's customer base, costly litigation, or revenue reductions.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the definition previously used by the Board in SR 95-51; commenters may discuss retaining, narrowing, or broadening this formulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'banking organization' (proposed)
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposal defines 'banking organization' to include a bank holding company (12 CFR 225.2(c)), a savings and loan holding company (12 CFR 238.2(m)), a state member bank (12 CFR 208.2(g)), the combined U.S. operations of a foreign banking organization (12 CFR 252.2 and 12 CFR 211.21(o)), and the direct and indirect subsidiaries of such entities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters are asked to consider whether to include additional categories (e.g., permitted payment stablecoin issuers) or exclude any categories and to explain legal and supervisory implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement of policy — non-encouragement/compulsion
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed policy statement: 'The Board shall not encourage or compel banking organizations to deny or condition the provision of banking or other financial products or services to an individual or business based on their constitutionally protected political or religious beliefs, associations, speech, or conduct, or based on involvement by the individual or business in politically disfavored but lawful business activities perceived to present reputation risk.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proposal also emphasizes that decisions to make loans or provide services rest with the banking organization acting in accordance with applicable law; it does not prohibit supervisory feedback to address other risk channels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on use of reputation risk in supervision
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board shall not use reputation risk as a component of its examination programs or in materials used for the supervision of banking organizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Materials used for supervision include examination manuals, guidance documents, and examiner training materials. This codifies removal of 'reputation' references from supervisory materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule of construction preserving enforcement authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in the section shall restrict the Board's authority to implement, administer, and enforce applicable law, including but not limited to BSA, OFAC sanctions programs, the Federal Reserve Act, Bank Holding Company Act, Home Owners' Loan Act, Change in Bank Control Act, International Banking Act, Bank Merger Act, International Lending Supervision Act, Federal Deposit Insurance Act, Equal Credit Opportunity Act, and Fair Housing Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Board will implement, administer, and enforce applicable law consistent with the policy and prohibition subsections; commenters may suggest additions or removals to the listed statutes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implementation: examiner training and internal management controls
rubrics_metrics.description: If finalized, the Board would provide training on all aspects of this proposal for supervisory staff and ensure internal management controls to oversee compliance with the proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters may provide views on appropriate training content, oversight mechanisms, or measures to ensure consistent implementation across institution types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paperwork Reduction Act (PRA) finding and requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the PRA, the Board may not conduct or sponsor, and a respondent is not required to respond to, an information collection unless it displays a valid OMB control number. The Board determined the proposal contains no collections of information under the PRA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters may address whether the proposed rule creates any indirect information-collection or reporting burdens not identified by the Board.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory Flexibility Act (RFA) content requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: For an initial regulatory flexibility analysis, the RFA requires inclusion of: (1) description of reasons for action; (2) objectives and legal basis; (3) description and estimate of number of small entities affected; (4) description of projected reporting/recordkeeping/compliance requirements and estimate of classes of small entities affected; (5) identification of relevant federal rules that may duplicate/overlap/conflict; and (6) description of significant alternatives that accomplish objectives while minimizing economic impact on small entities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Board provided an initial regulatory flexibility analysis and invites comment, particularly empirical data on impacts to small entities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Providing Accountability Through Transparency Act summary requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The Providing Accountability Through Transparency Act of 2023 requires that a notice of proposed rulemaking include the internet address of a summary of not more than 100 words in length of a proposed rule, in plain language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Board has posted the proposal and a summary on regulations.gov and its supervision/regulatory listing; commenters may comment on the adequacy of that summary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plain language solicitation
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board invites comment on whether it has used plain language and organized the material to suit readers' needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific questions include: Has the Board organized the material to suit your needs? Are the requirements clearly stated? Is there unclear technical jargon? Would a different format make it easier to understand? Which sections should be changed and how?
